oss.feature: indirect-addressing wall tables (solid/fluid boundary node lists + la_weight continuation + ISO8 wall normal)
oss.source_access: codeload tarball (588782 B) unpacked outside the repo; every conclusion carries file:line; no hand-copied numbers and no execution of the OSS binary (GPU/MPI/OpenACC build, and the inventory probe already recorded <1000-step NaN, docs/oss-inventory/oss-inv-lanl-MF-LBM.md sec. 9)

decision: Which wall-table representation and which wall-normal recipe TensorLBM should carry for near-wall FIELD operations, and whether the OSS ISO8 expression is transferable verbatim.

representation: A1: node-indexed indirect-addressing tables (MF-LBM solid_boundary/fluid_boundary lists, CSR-condensed) driving the near-wall field operators
A2: dense (Q, nz, ny, nx) mask + full-domain scan (the representation TensorLBM's dense BFL kernel uses today)
wall_normal: B1: projected ISO8 stencil, sum_s c_s sum_o o_alpha (phi(x+o)-phi(x-o))
B2: OSS-literal expression, sum_s c_s sum_o (phi(x+o)-phi(x-o)) (no o_alpha projection; Geometry_preprocessing.F90:236-378 verbatim)

hypotheses.H1_representation_identity: A1 and A2 produce bit-identical boundary operations: every KPI of the table-driven channel arm equals the dense-scan arm to < 1e-12 relative.
hypotheses.H2_normal_variant: B1 returns the exact normal of a plane wall (max component error < 1e-10) and mean |cos| > 0.99 against the radial direction on a D=24 sphere, while B2 (OSS literal) leaves transverse components > 0.3 on the plane wall and mean |cos| < 0.9 on the sphere.
hypotheses.H3_physics: The table-driven D3Q19 channel (half-way bounce-back from the link table, Guo forcing) reproduces the analytic Poiseuille u_max, superficial permeability and wall shear within the owner 15% band at H = 8, 16, 32.
hypotheses.H4_footprint: The CSR table pair costs less than 1/10 of the dense (Q, nz, ny, nx) mask + q-field for the sphere geometry, and also less than the OSS fixed-row layout (4 int32 + 18 int32 + 1 double per solid boundary node).
hypotheses.H5_continuation_semantics: The OSS la_weight continuation is exact for linear fields at the weight centroid of the fluid neighbours (machine precision) but is NOT a node extrapolation: applied to a channel velocity profile its output differs from the exact value at the solid node by more than 50%.

metrics.u_max_rel_err: |u_max_lbm - g*H^2/(8*nu)| / (g*H^2/(8*nu)), u_max taken over fluid cells at the last step
metrics.k_super_rel_err: superficial permeability k = nu*<u>_all_sites/g (mean over ALL cells of the cross-section, solid included) versus k_ref = (H/H_total)*H^2/12
metrics.tau_w_rel_err: wall shear from half-way bounce-back momentum exchange, F_wall/(nx*nz), versus rho*g*H/2
metrics.mass_drift: max |rho-1| over fluid cells at the last step
metrics.representation_rel: max relative difference between the table arm and the dense-scan arm over u_max, k_super, tau_w
metrics.normal_cos_mean/median/p05: cosine between the ISO8 normal and the exact radial/plane normal
metrics.table_bytes: bytes of the table pair (CSR int8 dir ids + int64 offsets + float64 weights) vs dense mask+q and vs the OSS fixed-row layout
metrics.boundary_op_seconds: one boundary-operation pass, table traversal versus dense scan

unit_of_analysis: one completed simulation arm at fixed (H, tau, steps) plus one static-geometry arm at fixed resolution; KPIs are scalars (fields for the normal statistics)

baseline_control.physical_baseline: analytic incompressible plane-channel Poiseuille flow driven by a body force: u(y)=g*y*(H-y)/(2*nu), u_max=g*H^2/(8*nu), tau_w=rho*g*H/2, k_super=(H/H_total)*H^2/12
baseline_control.representation_control: A2 dense-scan solver sharing collision, forcing, geometry, step count and steady-state criterion with A1; the only changed variable is how the boundary operations are addressed (table traversal vs full-domain mask scan)
baseline_control.normal_control: B2 OSS-literal stencil on the same smoothed indicator and the same evaluation cells as B1
baseline_control.oss_note: the OSS binary is not executed (CUDA/MPI/OpenACC, GPU absent; the inventory probe already recorded NaN within 1000 steps). The OSS semantics transplanted here are the table build, the la_weight continuation and the ISO8 normal, cited file:line; physical accuracy is measured against the analytic channel, not against an OSS run. This is recorded as a comparison limit.

predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: the 15% owner band is used only for physics-vs-analytic comparisons; representation identity is held to 1e-12 because a change of addressing must be exact, and stencil identities (normal on a plane wall, continuation of a linear field) are held to 1e-10/1e-12 because they are exact algebra, not discretisation
predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: a KPI is resolution-converged when |KPI(H=32)-KPI(H=16)|/|KPI(H=32)| < 5%; otherwise the finer value is reported together with the resolution delta as a sensitivity result
predeclared_thresholds.stability_rule: a run producing a non-finite population, rho outside [0.95,1.05] or Ma>0.1 is declared failed and reported, never tuned away

stopping_rule: each arm runs at most the step count fixed in run_arm.py (STEPS_MAX) and stops early only when the predeclared steady criterion max|u(n)-u(n-200)|/max|u(n)| < 1e-9 holds; no arm is extended after looking at KPIs. Per-arm wall clock budget 900 s; anything above goes to the cluster queue.
variables_changed: boundary addressing (A1 indirect-addressing tables / A2 dense mask scan)
channel resolution H = 8, 16, 32 fluid rows (ny = H+2), nx = nz = 4, periodic x and z
variables_held_fixed: D3Q19, BGK/SRT collision, Guo body force (velocity shift + source term), float64, single CPU thread, torch CPU
half-way bounce-back applied through the link table (q = 0.5, voxel geometry)
steady-state criterion and step budget identical across arms
geometry for the normal arms: plane wall in a 20x12x12 box and a sphere of radius n/4 centred in an n^3 box (n = 48)
confounders: half-way bounce-back places the wall 0.5 dx outside the first fluid row, so the analytic channel width must be H (not H+1); a geometric bias of 1/(H+0.5) otherwise appears (~12% at H=8)
the dense-scan control integrates the same arithmetic over the whole domain, so its cost is an upper bound for the addressing benefit, not a hardware-independent constant
the la_weight continuation is evaluated on the same smoothed indicator in both normal variants, so the difference between B1 and B2 is the stencil, not the smoothing
the ISO8 amplitude gain of the OSS coefficients is 0.99683 for the projected variant, i.e. a 0.32% scale bias survives in the normal magnitude but is removed by the normalisation
MF-LBM's y/z faces are walls and its x axis is periodic; the copy that wraps periodic axes therefore only reproduces OSS behaviour on the periodic directions
repetitions: every arm is deterministic (fixed initial condition u=0, rho=1, no randomness, no seeds); no repetition is averaged and no randomisation/blinding applies. The sampling unit is one arm, the spread across resolutions/tau is reported as sensitivity rather than as noise.
analysis: grouped by arm; no outlier removal; errors are relative to the analytic value (physics) or to the control arm (representation/stencil); uncertainty is the spread between H=16 and H=32 (and between tau values); footprint and timing are reported as ratios
fail_stage_plan: if the transplant fails, fail_stage names the stage (table_build / normal / continuation / boundary_op / channel_solver / analysis) and failure_reason carries the measured deviation; an honest FAIL is reported as such

amendments.what: run budget: STEPS_MAX 40000 -> 20000, steady tolerance 1e-9 -> 1e-7 over a 100-step window, channel cross-section nx=nz 4 -> 2, and the dense control arm (A2) plus the tau sweep are run at H<=16 while A1 covers H=8,16,32.
amendments.why: the first launch exceeded the 120 s per-command budget of this work tree (no KPI had been printed yet, so nothing was tuned against a result). nx=nz does not enter the physics -- the driven channel is homogeneous in x and z and periodic there -- and the steady tolerance is still 5 orders below the 5% convergence rule. The resolution/tau coverage that carries the acceptance decision (A1 at H=8,16,32 and the A1-vs-A2 identity control) is unchanged.

amendments.what: second run-budget amendment: physics arms are A1 at H=8 (4000 steps) and H=16 (8000 steps) plus the tau=0.6/1.0 sweep at H=16; the dense control A2 is folded into the same run as a final-state equivalence check (identical streamed field and identical momentum-exchange wall force, table traversal versus full-domain mask scan) instead of a second simulation; the continuation arm now uses H=16.
amendments.why: one arm costs ~3-4 ms/step in this work tree (~100 s for 20000 steps) and the per-command budget is 120 s. The A2 equivalence is an algebraic identity of the same state, so running a second simulation adds nothing; H=32 is dropped and the convergence ladder becomes H=8 -> H=16. The threshold set, the physics reference and the acceptance band are unchanged.
